name: Type IV Composite Gas Cylinders: Hydrogen, CNG Cascades & Lightweight Storage
scope: Carbon-fibre-wrapped, polymer-lined Type IV cylinders for hydrogen, CNG cascades and mobile gas storage are moving from import/pilot to Indian certification and first orders (Time Technoplast: PESO nod for 150L and 250L hydrogen cylinders and Rs 115 cr + Rs 88 cr PSU CNG-cascade orders in 2026; TDB-funded NTF CNG plant for 2027); only 3 small/mid-cap listed names confirmed, thinly covered by media, but Confidence Petroleum has already ~3x off its 52-week low (not clearly theme-driven) and Time Technoplast has not re-rated, so it is early-to-mid, with hydrogen volumes still pilot-scale.
questions: What are Type IV composite cylinders, how do they differ from Type I-III steel/aluminium-lined cylinders, and what are the key end uses (hydrogen mobility, CNG vehicles and cascades, industrial gas, SCBA)?
What is the current global demand outlook for Type IV hydrogen/CNG cylinders (market-research CAGR figures) and what is driving it in the last 1-3 months?
What regulatory and policy drivers exist in India (PESO approvals, TDB funding, National Green Hydrogen Mission, hydrogen blending in CNG, vehicle norms) and what is their timing?

What has Time Technoplast actually achieved (PESO approvals, Bureau Veritas certification, PSU CNG cascade orders, capex and capacity, hydrogen revenue timeline) and how material is it to group revenue and margins?

What is Confidence Petroleum's Type 4 project (Silversky Exim, Butibori Nagpur, claimed Rs 350 cr / 1-3 lakh units): has it been commissioned, certified, or generated revenue, and what is its financial and governance position?
What is Everest Kanto Cylinder doing in Type 4 (US subsidiary capex of USD 5.5 million, Type 3/4 positioning) and how much of it reaches Indian listed earnings?

Are there other Indian listed companies with confirmed Type IV, carbon-fibre-supply or composite-wrapping involvement (e.g. carbon fibre makers, CNG/hydrogen cascade makers), and what is the evidence for each?
How reliant is the value chain on imported carbon fibre, liners and valves, and which listed companies could capture that localisation?
Has the market priced this in: stock performance over 6-12 months, valuations, and broker/media coverage of the theme to date?

What are the main risks (slow hydrogen adoption, certification and customer qualification delays, competition from imports, execution, balance sheet quality) and what near-term catalysts (order wins, plant commissioning, PESO approvals, hydrogen-blending policy) should be tracked?

certified_manufacturers: Listed companies with approved Type IV products or firm orders in India
capacity_builders: Listed companies with publicly stated Type IV plants or capex but earlier-stage or unproven execution
